properties.title: A radiographic world model for clinical reasoning and evidence generation

membership.legacy_value: Exclude – non-temporal / static generative foundation model
membership.reason: Despite calling MedDream a 'radiographic world model' in the title, it is a static single-image masked autoregressive latent diffusion + CLIP alignment foundation model conditioned on radiology reports. It does not model temporal state transitions, action-conditioned rollouts, or longitudinal patient trajectories.
membership.counting_boundary: Excluded from core world models (not_world_model, BP_COMPONENT).

properties.backbone: Frozen CXR MedVAE + 636M Masked Autoregressive (MAR) Transformer + Continuous Diffusion Head + Clinical-T5-Large

properties.flow: Static CXR / radiology report -> MedDream shared continuous latent representation -> frozen-encoder linear probing / segmentation OR report-conditioned 512x512 CXR synthesis

properties.purpose: Chest radiograph diagnostic representation transfer, lesion localization, report-conditioned synthetic CXR generation, and subgroup rebalancing.
properties.environment: Multi-dataset retrospective benchmarks + retrospective UChicago reader studies

evidence_fragments.content: support both clinical readout and conditional simulation of radiographic observations. Here we introduce MedDream, a radiographic world model that learns a shared continuous latent state from paired chest radiograph–text observations for diagnostic reasoning and report-conditioned evidence generation. MedDream was pretrained on 2.65 million leakage-controlled chest radiograph–text pairs curated from 4.40 million candidates. Across eight clinical datasets and two independent reader cohorts, MedDream outperformed leading diagnostic and generative comparators. For

Figure 1:MedDream jointly learns a shared medical visual representation for diagnostic adaptation and reportconditioned evidence construction. a, Chest radiographs encode anatomical, pathological, acquisition-related, semantic and clinical-contextual information.b, Public chest-radiography data resources collected during corpus construction. Seven repositories contributed image–text pairs to the candidate corpus, whereas RALO was used only as an independent evaluation resource and did not contribute to MedDream pretraining.c, Literature-mining pipeline for extracting and curating candidate chest-radiograph image–caption pairs from open-access biomedical articles.d, Geographic distribution and source composition of the constructed chest-radiography image–text resource, including literature-mined PMC-CXR pairs and curated clinical image–text pairs before filtering to obtain the final leakagecontrolled pretraining corpus.e, MedDream jointly optimizes clinical image–text alignment and masked latent generation through the same continuous visual pathway. Both objectives update the shared image encoder, yielding a representation that supports frozen diagnostic adaptation and report-conditioned evidence construction.

Figure 2:Diagnostic representation transfer across clinical settings. a,Frozen-encoder linear-probing protocol. Chest radiographs were encoded by a fixed image encoder, standardized and passed to independent one-versus-rest binary classifiers.b,Mean AUROC on the NIH ChestX-ray14 hold-out test set for 14 common thoracic findings. Bars show model-level mean AUROC.c,Disease-wise rank trajectories on NIH ChestX-ray14 across evaluated thoracic findings. Lower rank indicates better disease-level performance.d,Disease-wise AUROC heat map on VinDr-CXR comparing MedDream with CheXzero, BiomedCLIP, RAD-DINO, MedKLIP, BMCA-CLIP, MedCLIP, Ark+ and AFLoc.e,Label-efficiency evaluation on ChestDR. Linear probes were trained with 5%, 10%, 25%, 50% or 100% of the labelled training set and evaluated by AUC for overall and disease-wise performance.

Figure 4:Report-conditioned generation and downstream synthetic-data experiments. a,Impression-conditioned generation quality evaluated by distributional fidelity and per-case metrics. FID was computed in XRV and CLIP feature spaces; pairwise MS-SSIM and Pearson correlation were computed at the case level.b, Feature-space analysis of real and generated images using XRV DenseNet121 features projected by t-SNE. Feature-space overlap was computed from two-dimensional density estimates.c, Blinded expert assessment of generated images using a five-point scale for image realism, acquisition plausibility and prompt-level consistency.d,Change in macro-AUROC after 1×and 2× synthetic augmentation on internal MIMIC-CXR and cross-dataset VinDr-CXR classification.e,Class-wise AUROC comparison across real-only training and synthetic augmentation with MedDream, ChexGen and MINIM.f,External VinDr-CXR AUROC by shared finding category after synthetic augmentation.g,Synthetic-pretraining experiment across real-data budgets. Models were pretrained on synthetic images and fine-tuned using 5%, 10%, 25%, 50% or 100% of the real training cohort.

MedDream uses a continuous-token masked autoregressive architecture for latent image modelling, following prior work on autoregressive image generation [18, 51, 52]. The model contains approximately 636 million trainable parameters, including a 201.5 million-parameter encoder. For latent image modelling, we used a frozen CXR-specific medical V AE implemented using the MedV AE architecture [53] to encode chest radiographs into latent representations and decode generated latents back into image space. The V AE was trained from scratch on the leakage-controlled training set without using the released MedV AE weights. For generative text conditioning, radiology reports or clinical prompts were encoded using Clinical-T5-Large, a T5-based clinical language model trained on MIMIC clinical notes [54]. Clinical-T5-Large served as the generation text encoderT g, whereas a separate alignment text encoderT ϕ was used for the CLIP-style image–text alignment branch. During training, the CXR V AE was kept frozen, and the masked autoregressive generator and text-alignment modules were optimized. We used AdamW with weight decay, an EMA decay of 0.9999, gradient clipping, and variable masking. The training objective combined the MAR reconstruction/generation loss with a lightly weighted CLIP-style image–text alignment loss. MedDream was trained on approximately 2.65 million leakage-controlled chest X-ray image–text pairs using eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Each epoch required approximately 53 minutes, and the full training run was conducted for 1,800 epochs, corresponding to an estimated training budget of about 12,720 A100 GPU-hours. The Stage 1 weights were then jointly refined at 512×512 resolution on MIMIC-CXR patient groups p10–p18, and the resulting Stage 2 EMA checkpoint was used for both primary diagnostic and generative evaluations. capability_assessments.rationale: Static single-image masked autoregressive latent diffusion + CLIP alignment foundation model conditioned on radiology reports; lacks temporal/action-conditioned state transition dynamics.

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R2/R3 External retrospective validation and reader studies

limitations: No temporal state transitions, longitudinal trajectory prediction, or action-conditioned rollouts (not a world model under Ontology 1.0.1).
Retrospective benchmarks and reader studies only; no prospective clinical deployment trial.
notes: All 39 physical PDF pages extracted and read; Figures 1-5 (pp. 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) visually inspected via rendered PNGs.

legacy_cells.B: A radiographic world model for clinical reasoning and evidence generation
legacy_cells.C: Xi, Suyang, Hu, Songtao, Wang, Shansong, Safari, Mojtaba, del Balzo, Luke, Karim, Ehsan Ul, et al.
legacy_cells.S: Can a shared chest-radiograph representation support diagnostic readout and report-conditioned generation of clinically aligned radiographic evidence?
legacy_cells.AI: Chest-radiograph images; paired clinical text, including radiology reports and impressions
legacy_cells.AJ: Pretrained CXR-specific VAE encoder; transformer image encoder; Clinical-T5-Large generation text encoder; separate, unnamed alignment text encoder
legacy_cells.AM: Shared image encoder/state jointly trained with image–text contrastive alignment and text-conditioned masked-latent generation
legacy_cells.BS: 512 × 512 report/impression-conditioned chest radiographs generated from masked continuous image latents
legacy_cells.BT: Frozen-feature disease and severity linear probes; lightweight lesion-segmentation head; downstream classifier and regressor
legacy_cells.BV: Masked-latent diffusion noise-prediction loss plus weighted bidirectional image–text contrastive loss (λ = 0.005)
legacy_cells.BY: Approximately 636 million trainable parameters, including a 201.5 million-parameter encoder
legacy_cells.CA: Stage 1: eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs, 1,800 epochs, about 53 minutes per epoch, estimated 12,720 A100 GPU-hours; Stage 2: six A100 GPUs for 200 epochs
legacy_cells.EE: Two independent reader cohorts are reported. In the severity-support experiment, three radiology residents each graded 100 held-out frontal CXRs unaided and, after washout, with model severity/confidence and synthetic references; independent radiologist consensus was the reference.
legacy_cells.EF: 3 radiology residents in the severity-support cohort; other reader cohort recorded separately in paper.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported results (source excerpt): For diagnostic reasoning, MedDream showed strong generalization across disease recognition, label-scarce adaptation, severity assessment, and localization, while MedDream-supported review increased mean resident concordance with independent radiologist consensus from 56.3% to 63.0%. For evidence generation, MedDream produced radiographs that preserved clinically relevant pathology and improved downstream performance on held-out real data, with synthetic augmentation increasing external VinDr-CXR macro-AUROC from 76.4% to 81.4%.
legacy_cells.FR: Radiograph representation, conditional image generation, external diagnostic transfer and reader agreement are demonstrated. These are not longitudinal patient-state forecasts, treatment-effect identification, or prospective patient-outcome effectiveness.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M2 Encoders; M3 Belief-state service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose the learned representation through a modality encoder/state interface, then independently validate next-state prediction before using it for simulation or control.
legacy_cells.FU: Reviewer mapping (KB §20): Incomplete multimodal state construction
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–39: title and abstract; Introduction; all Results (including Figs. 2–6); Discussion and limitations; Methods (data, architecture, training, evaluation and implementation); data availability; Supplementary Tables S1–S5; Extended Data Figs. 1–6. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Extraction relies on the complete local PDF text. The paper explicitly limits its implemented state to examination-level radiographs, not longitudinal patient-state dynamics; therefore the self-description as a world model is retained in W, but X is Not a world model and demonstrated capability is L0. Supplementary tables were inspected, but some extracted table rows (notably S1–S2) have disrupted column alignment; key filled fields are supported by narrative text and Methods. No external sources were consulted. Evidence QA: 22/30 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (73.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 29 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 1 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.
